outcomes.text: Skill 1.A: Recognize explicit meaning. (Interpretive Communication: Comprehend written texts, audio, and visualizations of data.)
Identify supporting or relevant details.
Identify data points, patterns, and trends.
Skill 1.B: Interpret meaning.
Determine the main idea, theme, or purpose.
Determine the intended audience.
Determine the point(s) of view, perspective(s), tone, or attitude.
Identify organizing and/or rhetorical structures and/or strategies.
Determine the meaning of words and phrases using textual cues.
Skill 1.C: Synthesize and infer meaning.
Connect information within or across sources.
Synthesize meaning to draw logical conclusions.
Infer implied meaning through context.

topics.title: Skill Category 2: Interpersonal and Presentational Communication

outcomes.text: Skill 2.A: Use language that aligns with the communicative purpose and context. (Interpersonal and Presentational Communication: Speak and write in interpersonal and presentational contexts.)
Use a variety of grammatical structures.
Use a variety of vocabulary.
Use idiomatic and culturally relevant expressions.
Adopt an appropriate register for the intended audience and situation.
Skill 2.B: Make communication comprehensible for the intended audience.
Use communication strategies such as circumlocution and paraphrasing.
Monitor language production; recognize errors and attempt self-correction in spoken exchanges.
Use pronunciation that is comprehensible to a variety of speakers of the target language.
Use an appropriate rate of speech and effective intonation patterns.
Use standard conventions of written language (e.g., capitalization, orthography, accents, punctuation).
Skill 2.C: Share ideas, information, and opinions about familiar and researched topics.
Express ideas, preferences, and opinions.
Use research strategies to gather information and evidence.
Use examples to provide advice or information and to explain opinions or emotions.
Integrate information from multiple sources to develop and support a position or perspective.
Reference and cite sources appropriately.
Skill 2.D: Apply organizational and rhetorical strategies.
Apply an appropriate organizational structure.
Use a variety of cohesive devices (e.g., relative pronouns, pronoun referents, conjunctions, transitions) to effectively convey and connect ideas.
Skill 3.A: Make connections within and across cultures. (Cultural Understanding: Demonstrate cultural understanding.)
Describe cultural products, practices, and perspectives.
Compare cultural products, practices, and perspectives among distinct communities.
Reflect on the significance of cultural products, practices, and perspectives.
Essential question: What constitutes a family in German-speaking societies? Wie versteht man den Begriff „Familie“ in deutschsprachigen Regionen?

Essential question: What are some important aspects of family values and family life in German-speaking societies? Was sind einige wichtige Aspekte und Werte des Familienlebens in deutschsprachigen Regionen?
Essential question: How do families and communities experience today’s world? Wie erleben Familien und Gemeinschaften die heutige Welt?
Students could: Explore how families shape values and traditions, as well as personal beliefs and interests.
Students could: Examine the experiences faced by families in modern society.
Students could: Consider the evolving role of the community in contemporary societies.

Other recommended instructional contexts: Customs and Celebrations; Linguistics; German in the World; Education and Career; Food and Health; Pop Culture; Global Communication; History; Policy and Planning.
